findings.title: Procedure omits the required summary toggle and reopen transitions
findings.evidence: Original target/verification-protocol.md:5-10 contains the full six-step procedure. Line 7 opens help with the summary but specifies no activation. Line 8 closes help using Close + Enter; the procedure then reaches Back without another help opening. surface-contract.json:11-13 requires summary Enter, summary Space, then summary Enter; line 18 requires help-toggle. Independent complete-source inspection and /workspace/output/roles/verifier/static-comparison.json show no Space step and no reopening step. The independently run checker exited 0 but its result explicitly covers contract consistency only; see /workspace/output/roles/verifier/contract-check.json.
findings.counterexample: Concrete static input: the supplied six-step verification-protocol.md (SHA-256 0a3452f02e358d8800fb26d591083deb972c5531165473990dc27007a9a9e0d4) evaluated against the supplied transition contract. Actual document result: open-help with activation unspecified, followed immediately by Close + Enter, followed by unanswered and Back assertions; zero instructions for summary + Space and zero instructions to reopen help. Expected: a help-open -> help-closed transition using summary + Space, followed by help-closed -> help-open using summary + Enter, as explicitly declared in contract lines 12-13, and explicit Enter for the initial opening at line 11. This actual static comparison demonstrates missing acceptance coverage in the document; it does not demonstrate a broken deployed control.
findings.refutation_attempt: Considered whether line 8 already satisfies help-toggle, or whether open-help implicitly includes the whole summary sequence. It cannot: line 8 names Close + Enter, while the contract distinguishes close-help from toggle-help and requires summary + Space. The single opening in line 7 cannot also occur after the later closure, because no subsequent opening appears in the complete procedure. Also tested whether the passing consistency checker proves procedure coverage: its code reads only the contract JSON, and its returned limit explicitly excludes browser behavior. These contrary checks do not refute the omission.
findings.triggering_condition: Use this document as the complete procedure for the supplied acceptance contract.
findings.practical_consequence: Completing the written steps cannot supply evidence for the required summary Space toggle and Enter reopening sequence.

findings.title: Procedure does not establish the required request-method and origin policies
findings.evidence: Original target/verification-protocol.md:1-10 contains only a fixture notice and six UI steps, with no network-control prerequisite, request observation, allowed-origin assertion, allowed-method assertion, or blocked-analytics effects record. surface-contract.json:5-6 permits only https://qaizen.io and GET/HEAD/OPTIONS; line 18 requires read-only-policy and origin-policy; line 20 requires retention of the expected blocked analytics POST effects. observation-policy.json:2-4 repeats the origin allowlist. Full-source inspection and the whole-word term comparison in /workspace/output/roles/verifier/static-comparison.json independently establish the document omission. Independently run checker output is in /workspace/output/roles/verifier/contract-check.json; it explicitly limits itself to contract consistency.
findings.counterexample: Concrete static input: the complete supplied six-step procedure and contract policies allowed_origins=[https://qaizen.io], allowed_methods=[GET,HEAD,OPTIONS], required_checks including read-only-policy and origin-policy, plus the blocked-analytics effects requirement. Actual document result: the procedure starts navigation at line 5, performs UI actions/assertions through line 10, and ends without specifying or referencing any policy setup/precondition, request-policy evidence, or blocked-analytics effects record. Expected document coverage: establish the declared method/origin constraints for observation, check those policies, and retain observed effects of the expected blocked analytics POST. This comparison demonstrates an actual document completeness defect. No analytics POST, redirect, prohibited request, successful UI trace, or deployed website behavior was executed or observed.
findings.refutation_attempt: Considered whether opening the public entry in line 5 establishes origin-policy, and whether leaving answers unanswered in lines 6, 9-10 establishes read-only-policy. The former identifies a starting destination only; it says nothing about subsequent request origins. The latter constrains questionnaire input only; it does not state allowed HTTP methods, policy checks, or blocked POST effects. Checked the complete document for an inherited-controls prerequisite or reference and found none. observation-policy.json supplies an allowlist declaration, not evidence that this procedure establishes or checks it. The checker inspects the contract only and therefore cannot cure the procedure omission. An externally preconfigured browser could constrain traffic, but none was observed and it would not supply this document with its missing required checks/effects record. Thus the static omission is confirmed; candidate illustrations of actual network side effects remain unobserved.
findings.triggering_condition: Use this document as the complete procedure for the supplied origin/read-only acceptance obligations.
findings.practical_consequence: The completed procedure supplies no specified evidence for the mandatory network policy checks and blocked-analytics effects record.
